content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Write equations for reactions with hydrogen, water, and halogens
Understand the mechanism of electrophilic addition
The C=C double bond in alkenes is reactive and undergoes
. In these reactions, the double bond "opens up" and atoms add to the two carbon atoms. This is the basis for making many useful products.
Atoms/groups add to the two carbon atoms
[DIAGRAM: General addition reaction showing C=C + X-Y → C-C with X and Y attached]
Alkene reacts with Cl₂, Br₂, or I₂
This is the test for unsaturation:
Alkenes react with HCl, HBr, HI:
The electron-rich C=C attracts the electrophile (e.g., Br₂)
The double bond breaks, one carbon bonds to Br, forming a carbocation
The second Br⁻ bonds to the positively charged carbon
[DIAGRAM: Mechanism showing curly arrows for bromine addition to ethene]
atoms add across the double bond
When HX adds to an unsymmetrical alkene:
H adds to the carbon with more hydrogens already attached
X adds to the carbon with fewer hydrogens
Write the equation for the reaction of propene with hydrogen.
The double bond opens and H₂ adds across it
Describe how ethanol is made industrially from ethene.
Ethene is reacted with steam (water vapour)
The process is reversible; not all ethene converts
Name the product when but-1-ene reacts with chlorine.
Chlorine adds across the double bond
Cl₂ becomes two Cl atoms, one on each carbon
Explain why vegetable oils are hydrogenated to make margarine.
Vegetable oils contain unsaturated fats (C=C bonds)
These make the oil liquid at room temperature
Adding hydrogen (H₂) across the double bonds creates saturated fats
Saturated fats have higher melting points
The hydrogenated fat is solid at room temperature
This makes it spreadable as margarine
Conditions: nickel catalyst, heat, hydrogen gas
Confusing hydration (adding H₂O) with hydrogenation (adding H₂)
Hydration makes alcohols; hydrogenation makes alkanes
Forgetting the catalyst in reaction conditions
Ni for hydrogenation; H₃PO₄ for hydration
Thinking bromine water test shows a reaction with alkanes
Alkanes don't react with bromine water (stays orange)
Double bond opens, atoms add to both carbons
